title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body — 40-Minute Lesson Plan
subject: Science
chapter_title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
objectives: Identify the major food groups and their main role in the body.
Explain why a balanced diet is essential for growth and health.
Plan a simple balanced meal using available local foods.
Recognise common deficiency diseases (scurvy, rickets, anaemia, goitre).
prerequisites: Can name a few foods eaten in their region.
materials: Pictures of staple foods (rice, dal, vegetables, fruits, milk, ghee)
Iodine drops, plain paper, a peanut or piece of butter (for fat test demo)
A boiled potato slice and bread (for starch test demo)

activities.description: Quick poll: 'What did you eat for breakfast today?' Tally answers on the board. Ask: 'Which of these gives you energy? Which helps you grow?' Lead into the day's topic.
student_actions: Try to guess which foods serve which purpose

activities.description: Demo two simple food tests: (a) iodine on a slice of boiled potato — colour turns blue-black, indicating starch. (b) Rub a peanut on plain paper, hold it up to light — translucent oil patch, indicating fat. Students record observations.
teacher_actions: Ask what each test tells us
student_actions: Connect each test to its food group

activities.description: Mini-lecture: introduce the food-component table — carbohydrates (energy), proteins (growth), fats (long-lasting energy), vitamins/minerals (protection), fibre (digestion), water (every body process). Use one local food example for each. Then introduce the idea of balanced diet.
teacher_actions: Draw the food-component table on the board
student_actions: Add a personal example for each row

activities.description: Pair work: each pair plans a balanced one-day menu using foods their family eats. They mark which food group each item satisfies. Two pairs share their plan with the class.
student_actions: Tag each item with its food group

activities.description: Quick check on deficiency diseases: 4 oral questions — symptom -> deficiency -> food to add. (Bleeding gums -> vitamin C -> citrus / amla; tired and pale -> iron -> spinach / dal; bowed legs in young child -> vitamin D / calcium -> milk + sunlight; swollen neck -> iodine -> iodised salt.)
teacher_actions: Probe for the food source as well as the nutrient

activities.description: Homework: each student writes a 'food log' for one full day — everything they ate and drank — and tags each entry with its main food group. They will compare logs in pairs next class.
student_actions: Plan to record after each meal

homework: One-day food log with food-group tags.
Read the chapter summary on the Learn page and answer 3 takeaway questions in your notebook.
assessment_ideas: Use 5 questions from the bank: 1 on naming components, 1 on balanced diet, 1 on a deficiency disease, 1 short-answer planning a meal, 1 evaluating a sample meal.
Class chart: stick photos of 'protective', 'energy-giving', 'body-building' foods around the room.
Pair quiz: one student names a food, the other names its main food group.
references: NCERT Class 6 Science 'Curiosity', Chapter 3: Mindful Eating
Chapter summary and mind map on the Learn page
ICMR-NIN dietary guidelines for Indian children (background reading for the teacher)
